newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- The U.S. government is trying to find ways to get recipients of its money like military contractors to accept payment electronically and not in the form of paper checks.
- Japan is forming consortia and cooperatives between public and private sectors to gain leadership in the semiconductor industry.
- By dumping McDonnell Douglas Corp, the Pentagon is showing it is ready to do more business with civilian companies with a more diverse customer base.
- Black motorists are still doing business with Texaco Inc stations despite a boycott called by civilian activists.
- The executive in charge of the operating systems division at Apple Computer Inc has resigned.
- Primeco Personal Communications is competing financially and technically with AT&T Wireless Services for personal communications services.
- Airline ValuJet Inc and maintenance contractor Sabretech are to appear this week at hearings held by National Transportation Safety Board hearings about last May's crash.
- Casio Computer Co Ltd, Compaq Computer Corp, Hewlett-Packard Co and Philips Electronics HV are presenting computers the size of paperbacks at the Comdex computer trade show.
- Britain and the United States are easing restrictions on telephone competition.
